text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:
- Unemployment in Switzerland fell for the first time in eight months to 5.6 percent from 5.7 percent in February. At the end of March some 202,000 people were officially jobless.
- The Worldwide Fund for Nature in Gland, Switzerland announced a new plan of action that calls for governments to protect at least 10 percent of forests by the year 2,000.
- The Fotolabo Group achieved a huge jump in sales of 53 percent to 307 million Swiss francs in 1996, mainly due to recent acquisitions.
- Accounting and consulting group Atag Ernst & Young posted a six percent consolidated profit rise to 12.3 million Swiss francs in 1996.
- Winterthur Insurance named 42-year-old Thomas Wellauer as its new head of the board of directors.
- Rieter Group's sales rose by 9.6 percent to 2.2 billion Swiss francs in 1996.
- Economists at the Federal Institute of Technology (ETH) expect the rising trend in Swiss unemployment to continue and reach over six percent by next year.
- The University of Geneva said it has discovered a substance that fights against the AIDS virus.
